title_en: Lebanese Code of Commerce: merchants, companies, cheques and bankruptcy
title_ar: قانون التجارة البرية اللبناني: التاجر والشركات والشيك والإفلاس
question_en: What does the Lebanese Code of Commerce say about who is a merchant, registration, companies, cheques and bills of exchange, and bankruptcy?
question_ar: ماذا يقول قانون التجارة البرية اللبناني عن صفة التاجر والسجل التجاري والشركات والشيك وسند السحب والإفلاس؟
sub_questions: Who counts as a merchant and which acts are commercial?
Do I have to register in the commercial register and how soon?
Which commercial books must a merchant keep and for how long?
What are the main company types and what is the minimum capital of a joint-stock company?
What must a cheque contain and within how many days must it be presented?
When is a merchant declared bankrupt and what happens to acts done before?
notes: LAW: Code of Commerce (land commerce), Legislative Decree 304 of 24/12/1942, id 244586. The cheque is spelled 'شك' in the database text (Arts. 409 to 445); the bill of exchange is 'سند السحب'. The database does NOT hold in this code a penal article for cheques without funds (the bounced-cheque criminal offence is not in this text) so the page must not describe criminal penalties for a bounced cheque. The limited liability company (SARL) is not regulated by this code (separate law, not in the pack): say so. Art. 83 sets a joint-stock company minimum capital of 30 million LL as enacted/amended (old pounds); do not present it as a current dollar value. Art. 16 (books) includes a digital-books provision added by amendment. Cheque time limits: presentation within 8 days in Lebanon (Art. 426); claims against drawer and endorsers lapse 6 months after the presentation period (Art. 442); bill of exchange claims against the acceptor lapse after 3 years (Art. 398). Art. 10 exempts petty traders from books and publicity rules. Bankruptcy: Art. 489 defines it, Art. 507 lists acts void if done after the cessation of payments or in the 20 days before. Articles 40 and 41 are repealed (replaced by decree-law 11/1967 on the commercial establishment), do not cite them.

pack.why: Commercial acts, acts of a merchant, who is a merchant, small traders exempt
Commercial books, ten-year retention, books as evidence
Registration of a merchant (within one month) and of a company in the commercial register
Companies: written contract, legal personality, partnership, partner status, minimum capital of a joint-stock company
Limitation of three years on bill of exchange claims against the acceptor
Cheque: contents, drawee must be a banker holding funds, payable on sight, presentation in 8 days, six-month limitation
Bankruptcy: definition, declaration by the court, loss of administration, void acts in the suspect period
